q1.a: From your tariff: the per-kilometre rate for the coach class, the driver day rate, tolls and fuel, plus a fixed base fee. The distance includes intermediate stops, the return leg and day trips from the destination, and when the route passes the daily driving limit a second driver is priced in as well.

q2.q: What if the group picks people up in several places?
q2.a: Add as many intermediate stops as you need. Each one counts towards the route, the distance and the driving time, and the customer sees them drawn on the map before confirming the booking.

q3.q: Is the passenger count in the enquiry binding?
q3.a: No. The number of passengers is used to suggest the right coach class. The exact count is confirmed before departure, and if the group changes significantly the price is recalculated.

q4.q: Do we need our own website?
q4.a: Not necessarily. BusFlow ships with a public site — home, services, contact and the trip planner — styled to your brand. If you already have a website, the planner and booking flow can be embedded into it.

q5.a: The customer pays by card when booking and the money goes straight to your account through the payment provider. Schools and companies can pay against an invoice or a deposit instead.

q6.a: A basic installation with your tariff and branding is set up in a few days. After that we walk through the system together and migrate any existing data.

scope.label: Scope
scope.value: Website, booking system and admin area

challenge.title: Every enquiry was manual work
challenge.sub: Before BusFlow the path from enquiry to confirmed trip ran through the phone, email and a calculator.

c1.title: Enquiries arrive incomplete
c1.desc: Phone and email bring half the information — no exact route, dates or group size. A round of back-and-forth has to happen before anything can be priced.

c2.title: Prices are worked out by hand
c2.desc: Distance, driver day rates, tolls and fuel for every variant, one at a time. The answer takes hours or days, and by then the group has asked someone else.

c3.title: No overview
c3.desc: Bookings, payments and seat availability live in spreadsheets and messages, so the state of the fleet is hard to see in one place.

solution.title: What we built
solution.sub: The public site and the internal system are one application — what the customer types is immediately data in the admin area.

s1.title: Trip planner
s1.desc: Departure, intermediate stops, destination and day trips from the destination, with the route drawn on a map and distance and driving time calculated automatically.

s2.title: Instant price
s2.desc: The price comes from the operator’s tariff: per-kilometre rates by coach class, driver day rates, tolls and fuel. Long routes automatically get a second driver under the EU driving-time rules.

s3.title: Online booking
s3.desc: The customer confirms their details and the booking with the full itinerary — route, stops, day trips, dates and group size land in the system straight away.

s4.title: Tickets for scheduled departures
s4.desc: Published lines with capacity and ticket price, individual seat sales and live occupancy.

s5.title: Admin area
s5.desc: Bookings, departures, tariff, payments and users with roles — owner, administrator and staff see exactly what they are allowed to.

s6.title: Three languages and secure sign-in
s6.desc: The whole platform in German, English and Croatian, emails included. Sign-in runs through Keycloak, with two-factor authentication and Google sign-in.

s7.title: Card payment through myPOS
s7.desc: Payment runs through myPOS Checkout: the system builds a signed payment form and verifies the signature on the callbacks before marking a booking paid. Confirmation arrives both server-to-server and through the browser, so it is handled idempotently — a duplicate message cannot create a duplicate payment. Refunds are recorded against the booking.
